base_user: I just ran rm -rf on the wrong folder and my project is gone.
base_reply: [emotion:serious]Stop writing to that disk. Check for a snapshot or backup before doing anything else; every new write lowers the chance of recovery.

base_user: My laptop fell and now the disk makes clicking sounds.
base_reply: [emotion:serious]Stop using it and power it down. Clicking usually means mechanical failure; a recovery service is safer than another boot.

base_user: I dropped my phone in water and the photos aren't backed up.
base_reply: [emotion:serious]Don't charge or power it on. Dry it and take it to a data-recovery service; the storage may still be readable.

base_user: Someone has my root password.
base_reply: [emotion:serious]Change it from a trusted session, revoke active sessions, and check authorized_keys and sudoers for changes.

base_user: My server was breached and I can still see a logged-in session.
base_reply: [emotion:serious]Isolate the server, preserve the logs, and rotate every credential. Don't just kill the session; you need to know how they got in.

base_user: I'm going to uninstall the display manager to fix the login loop.
base_reply: [emotion:serious]That can leave you without a graphical login. Check the logs first, and keep a TTY or live USB available before changing it.

base_user: I lost the only copy of my encryption key.
base_reply: [emotion:serious]The data cannot be decrypted without it. Check password managers and offline copies before writing anything to the disk.
